coder-brief-slice-three-the-in-window-ro.text: Coder brief, slice three: the in-window rows.
The whole of slice three for the commit owner, with its terminal condition. The binding and limits are in the mandate; the proof is the gate. Slices one and two are on the branch.

story.text: As a reader of the public conformance suite, I see the rows about rejecting a request inside its windows say exactly what is true until the validators change: which rejection the model and the chain both accept, which one the model refuses while the chain still accepts it, labelled unmet and never as a pass, and what will turn that label into agreement.

direction.text: Decision B of 9 October 2026 (operator ruling, recorded in the mandate): this ticket merges alone, ahead of ticket 495. After it the suite shows two rows.
The rejection at once, with lifecycle evidence, of a request that cannot be folded: model and chain both accept and the owner is refunded. Green.

The rejection, inside the windows, of a foldable insertActive request for a key not yet registered: the model refuses, the chain accepts. Published as unmet by ruling and never counted as passing. A tripwire turns red unless ticket 495 changes the validators so that the two agree; ticket 495's acceptance includes that flip.

The row books a foldable insertion on a fresh key, because the insertion the standing row books today names an edge the two-edge model excludes, which is rejectable at once and would leave the row without its subject.

rulings-this-slice-implements.text: The operator's words, verbatim; the rest of the rulings are in the mandate.
A lifecycle mismatch permits immediate rejection:
Authenticated incompatibility with the current lifecycle state permits immediate rejection even when a later transition could make the request eligible.
expiry-only rejection after both the processing and owner's reclaim windows end ... The expiry threshold is therefore submission time plus processing duration plus reclaim duration.
A request naming an excluded edge is rejectable at once:

Epic owner ruling of 9 October 2026, as an application of the first ruling: an excluded edge has no successor at any leaf, so a request naming one is incompatible with every current state and is rejectable at once with the lifecycle evidence.

seat.text: You are not alone in the codebase; do not revert edits made by others. No Co-Authored-By, no attribution. Plain words, no coined abbreviations.

the-task.text: The dedicated early-rejection row ("early rejection inside the windows") becomes a lawful rejection that model and chain both accept inside the windows: a request to register a key that is already Active, rejected at once with the lifecycle evidence, the owner refunded the deposit. Its tampered refunds (one lovelace short, to another key) stay refused by both for the refund reason. Its workflow assertions and placement counts follow the row; its name and requirement text are unchanged.

The generic session's standing unmet row for rejecting a request while it can still be folded books a foldable registration, an insertion of a key not yet registered (a request naming a retired edge is rejectable at once and would leave the row without its subject), and records each of its three steps as the divergence it now is: the two refund controls refuse for different reasons, the untampered reject is refused by the model and accepted by the chain. Its stated reason and consumer reading change to say that the model refuses and the chain does not; its standing stays unmet. The session's expected-debt assertion keeps naming exactly the same rows.

The tripwire: the row's expected list stops matching, and the session goes red, on the day the chain refuses the untampered reject. Prove it with a seeded control in the same way the neighbouring rows prove theirs, or say in the receipt why the existing control already covers it.
The consumer record, the book and the evidence page say the same, including the history of ticket 320's early rejection. History is not edited; add a dated note, do not rewrite.
Regenerate what the prose moves: speech companions and audio of the edited pages, the row inventory.

checkpoints.text: Journal REVIEW-REQUESTED with commit and evidence path, and continue, at: the red-for-the-right-reason control (the rows as they stand fail against the changed model); the dedicated row green; the unmet row recorded; the final head.

gate.text: The slice-three rows of the gate: the two devnet rows locally once each, the non-devnet conformance commands, format and lint, the workflow lint and the documents check. The running book, the generic rows and the refusal extent check, moved here from slice two (gate version 2), run once on the final candidate after the two rows above.

terminal-condition.text: Stop at the first of: every slice-three gate command exits as the gate states on a clean committed head (CANDIDATE-GREEN); a question the mandate cannot decide (user story per option, BLOCKED); capacity (COMPLETE capacity-limit with a handoff). Touch nothing under the files this ticket must not touch.
